lines.text: It's Black Friday. Ever wonder how those store gates know you didn't pay?
Many security stickers hide two thin metal strips. One is a special alloy that vibrates in a magnetic field. The other is a magnet that tunes it.
The gates send out short bursts at fifty eight kilohertz, and the strip starts vibrating, like a tiny tuning fork.
When each burst stops, the strip keeps ringing, and the gate hears it. Beep.
At checkout, the cashier swipes it over a pad that demagnetizes the magnet strip, so the tag goes quiet.
Other tags use a tiny coil and capacitor tuned to eight point two megahertz, and get fried at checkout instead.
